# v1.1.0-dev.61 — Your Parsec display keeps its settings

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.60`.

Two things: a real bug where a Parsec virtual display forgot its
display settings on every reconnect, and a resolution picker that
had grown to 229 entries on one dropdown.

## The Parsec Display Kept Forgetting

If you set up a zoom to resolution rule for a Parsec virtual
display in dev.60, it worked once and then quietly stopped
working the next time you connected.

Windows gives a monitor a long hardware path, and WLM used the
whole thing to remember which display a setting belonged to. That
is fine for a monitor plugged into your graphics card. It is not
fine for a Parsec virtual display, because part of that path is
regenerated every single time Parsec creates the display. Next
session, the setting was filed under a name that no longer
existed, so nothing matched and nothing applied.

There was a second half to this. When the exact path did not
match, WLM fell back to the monitor's reported name. On most
machines every display reports the same name, "Generic PnP
Monitor", so that fallback matched *everything*. One monitor's
rule could apply to a completely different monitor.

Both are fixed. Settings are now filed under the part of the
hardware path that does not regenerate, which is stable across
Parsec sessions and still different for each monitor model. The
useless generic name is no longer used to identify anything, ever.

If you had a rule that stopped working, set it once more and it
will stay.

## WLM Can Tell Your Displays Apart Now

Windows reports two levels of information about a display, and
WLM was only reading the one that says "Generic PnP Monitor" for
everything. The other level is the one that says "Parsec Virtual
Display Adapter" or "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090".

WLM reads both now. Practically:

- Your monitor rows are no longer three identical lines. They
  show the resolution, and a virtual display says so.
- Parsec displays are recognised properly, rather than by looking
  for the word "parsec" somewhere in a device path.

## The Resolution List Got Usable

One display on the test machine offers 227 modes. As a single
dropdown that was 229 entries, which is not a menu, it is a
scrolling exercise.

It is now two dropdowns, the way Windows and NVIDIA both do it.
One for size, one for refresh rate. Sizes are grouped by shape
(16:9, 4:3, portrait), the one your display runs natively is
marked, and the old small sizes hide behind **Show every size**.
Nothing was removed, it is one click away.

229 entries became 20.

Picking a size that cannot do your current refresh rate keeps the
rate when it can and otherwise falls back to the highest that
size offers, and tells you it did. It no longer silently jumps to
whatever was first in the list.

**By hand** is still there for a resolution your display does not
list yet, and a saved resolution your current display cannot do
now shows up filled in and flagged, rather than as an empty box
that looks like you never set anything.

## Also

Dropdown menus are dark now. They had been opening as white
rectangles against the dark theme, which was one line of CSS the
whole time.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
